title: How to Bake Sourdough Flatbread on a Baking Sheet
meta_description: Learn the foolproof sourdough flatbread oven method using a baking sheet and silicone baking mats for crisp, non‑stick results every time.
html:
When you’ve got a lively starter and a craving for something chewy yet crisp, the sourdough flatbread oven method is the quickest way to satisfy that urge. All you need is a baking sheet, a little flour, and a reliable non‑stick surface – like our Silicone Baking Mats – to keep the dough from sticking and the cleanup to a minimum.

Why the Baking Sheet Beats the Cast‑Iron Skillet

A baking sheet spreads heat evenly across the dough’s base, creating a uniform crust without the hot spots you often get with a cast‑iron skillet. The flat, open surface also lets you fit multiple flatbreads on one pan, which is perfect for family meals or meal‑prep. Pair the sheet with a silicone baking mat and you’ve got a non‑stick, reusable alternative to parchment that tolerates high oven temps without tearing.

Gather Your Ingredients and Tools

Everything you need is pantry‑friendly. Here’s a quick checklist:

  1. 150 g active sourdough starter (100 % hydration)
  2. 200 g all‑purpose flour
  3. 100 g whole‑wheat flour (optional for extra flavor)
  4. 150 ml lukewarm water
  5. 1 tsp salt
  6. Olive oil for brushing
  7. Silicone Baking Mats (our recommended non‑stick surface)
  8. Baking sheet (rimmed, 13×18 in works well)
  9. Bench scraper and kitchen towel

Having the mat ready before you preheat the oven saves you a step – just lay it on the sheet and let it heat along with the pan.

Mix, Rest, and Shape: The Core of the Sourdough Flatbread Oven Method

Start by whisking the starter, water, and both flours together in a large bowl until no dry spots remain. The dough will be shaggy and a bit sticky; that’s normal. Cover the bowl with a damp towel and let it rest for 30 minutes – this autolyse period lets the flour hydrate fully and makes the later stretch easier.

After the rest, sprinkle salt over the dough and fold it in with a wet hand. The dough should feel slightly tacky but manageable. Transfer it onto a lightly floured surface, pat it into a rough rectangle, and let it sit for another 10 minutes.

Now comes the shaping: using a bench scraper, cut the dough into 4‑6 equal pieces (depending on how big you want your flatbreads). Lightly flour each piece, then stretch or roll each into a ¼‑inch thick circle or oval. If the dough springs back, let it rest for a minute and try again – the gluten is still developing.

Bake: High Heat and a Quick Turn

Preheat your oven to 475°F (245°C) with the baking sheet inside. A hot sheet is the secret behind that crisp bottom. When the oven screams it’s ready, carefully slide the silicone baking mat (with the flatbreads already placed on top) onto the sheet. Brush the tops lightly with olive oil – this adds flavor and helps the edges brown.

Slide the sheet back into the oven and bake for 6‑8 minutes, or until the edges are golden and the surface shows a few puffed spots. For an extra‑crisp finish, you can flip the flatbreads halfway through using a spatula and bake an additional 2 minutes on the other side.

Once out of the oven, let the flatbreads rest on a wire rack for a minute. The silicone baking mat makes this step a breeze; you can simply lift the mat and slide the breads off without any sticking.

Serving Ideas and Storage Tips

These sourdough flatbreads are incredibly versatile. Use them as a base for quick pizzas, slice them for finger‑food sandwiches, or serve alongside hummus and olives for a simple appetizer. If you have leftovers, store them in a zip‑top bag at room temperature for up to two days – the mat’s non‑stick surface helps keep them from drying out.

To re‑crisp, pop them back in a 350°F oven for 3‑4 minutes or toast them in a skillet for a minute per side. The silicone baking mat can also be used for reheating, ensuring the breads don’t cling to the pan.

Cleaning Up Without the Scrub

One of the biggest wins of the sourdough flatbread oven method is the cleanup. After the bread has cooled, simply peel the silicone baking mat off the sheet, rinse it under warm water, and wipe it clean with a non‑abrasive sponge. No parchment to toss, no grease baked into the pan – just a quick rinse and the mat is ready for the next bake.

FAQ

Can I use whole‑wheat flour only?

Yes, but expect a denser texture. Mixing whole‑wheat with all‑purpose flour gives you the best balance of flavor and chew.

Do I need to pre‑heat the baking sheet?

Absolutely. A hot sheet creates that characteristic crisp bottom and shortens bake time, which is key to the sourdough flatbread oven method.

Is the silicone baking mat dishwasher‑safe?

It is. The mat can be placed on the top rack of the dishwasher, or you can hand‑wash it. Either way, it stays non‑stick and ready for repeated use.
